title: Embodied Intelligence: Definition, Clarification, Criteria, and Boundaries（具身智能：定义、澄清、判据与边界）
description: Seventh paper of the human-referential fitting theory program. Between 2024 and 2026, "embodied intelligence" grew from a term in robotics and cognitive science into a word shared by policy documents, industry publicity, and academic surveys in many countries, without acquiring a stable definition; its parallel English names, embodied AI and physical AI, are in the same case. This paper extends the conceptual toolkit of the human-referential fitting theory to that term. (1) Definition: embodiment is a relational property of a system and an environment. A system S is embodied relative to an environment E if and only if its actions change the state of E through physical causation and its feedback comes from physical measurement (the physical closed loop), and its response latency lies below the characteristic time of the task-relevant physical process in E (timing prescribed by the environment). Embodied intelligence is the conjunction of two independent predicates, "embodied" and "intelligent"; it constitutes no new concept type but a restricted case of the capacity concept over physical environment classes. (2) Clarification: censuses of the English- and Chinese-language definitional corpus show that the existing disagreements have three sources: one limb of the conjunction written into the definition, the environment class left undeclared, and the level of the word left undistinguished. The three illicit slides each reappear in this discourse, joined by a fourth specific to it: conjunction confusion. (3) Criteria: the two conditions yield four executable tests (the closed-loop test, the body-swap test, the rollback test, and the pause test), and the timing margin gives a quantitative reading of "weak embodiment". (4) Distinctions and evidence: embodied intelligence implies neither the machine mind nor the world model; the claim that embodied intelligence is the road to AGI holds as a capacity claim but is not a conceptual inference as a route claim; and evidence from policy, think-tank, and corporate texts shows that systems which are embodied but lack the capacity, and systems which have the capacity but are not embodied, are both given the name. Seven falsifiability clauses, an admission protocol for new cases, and a survival clause close the paper.
